notes.1: SOURCE: Keysight 3458A Multimeter data sheet 5965-4971E (published June 10, 2026), supplied as hp3458a_specs.pdf; printed page numbers equal the PDF page numbers: DC volts p. 12 (transfer accuracy p. 13), resistance pp. 16-17, DC current p. 20, AC volts pp. 24 (SYNC), 27 (ANA), 29 (RNDM), AC current p. 32, frequency / period p. 34. Built by specs/build_3458a_standard.py.
notes.2: VERIFICATION: every stored number was read from RENDERED PAGE IMAGES (never the extracted text), each table twice (whole page, then a 300 dpi crop of the table); the two readings agree. Notes that only quote the temperature coefficients of the AC functions, the ACDCV / ACDCI additional errors and the frequency / period characteristics were read once (information; no lookup uses them). The 1 GOhm resistance temperature coefficient WITH ACAL (printed "1   2") could not be read in the data sheet itself and is NOT stored.
notes.3: CONFIDENCE LEVEL: NOT STATED. The data sheet (pp. 8-35) prints no confidence level, sigma, coverage factor k, or "99 %" / "95 %"; p. 8 says only that the accuracy is relative to the calibration standards. Stored as confidence_pct None ("[Not Specified]"), so the repository rule for such a sheet applies: coverage divisor 2.0 ASSUMED (the same treatment as the 8563E, 8902A and 96270A sheets). Set the divisor in Standards Specs if the lab decides otherwise (a Keysight spec limit is often treated as a rectangular limit, divisor sqrt(3), but this sheet does not say so).
notes.4: RELATIVE vs ABSOLUTE (p. 8): all accuracy specifications are RELATIVE to the calibration standards. The absolute accuracy adds the traceability error of the standards used for the last external calibration; the data sheet gives the factory figure and it is NOT added to any stored row: DC volts +2 ppm of reading (p. 12 footnote 5), resistance +3 ppm of reading, traceability of 10 kOhm (p. 16 footnote 3), DC current +5 ppm of reading, the sum of the 10 V and 10 kOhm values (p. 20 footnote 5), AC volts +2 ppm of reading, traceability of 10 V DC (pp. 24, 27), AC current +5 ppm of reading (p. 32 footnote 2). When the lab calibrates its own 3458A the traceability of THAT calibration replaces these factory figures. OPEN ITEM: the owner is unsure whether the factory adders should be added; they stay NOT stored until decided.
notes.5: RANGE (p. 8): "Range means the name of the scale, e.g., 1 V, 10 V, etc.; range does not mean the full-scale reading, e.g., 1.2 V, 12 V". The ppm / % of range term is therefore taken against the range NAME (0.1 V on the 100 mV range, 1 V, 10 V, 100 V, 1000 V; 1 uA on the 1 uA range ...), stored as fs_value; the row spans -full scale to +full scale (full scale as printed: 120 mV, 1.2 V, 12 V, 120 V, 1050 V; resistance 12 ohm ... 1.2 Gohm; DC current 120 nA ... 1.05 A; AC volts 12 mV ... 120 V and 700 V on the 1000 V range; AC current 120 uA ... 1.05 A).
notes.6: PERIODS (owner: the lab uses 1 year specifications): only "90 day" and "1 yr" are stored (the printed 24 hour and 2 year columns are NOT stored); the default period of the standard is "1 yr". Conditions: 90 day / 1 year = within 24 hours and +/-1 degC of the last ACAL, Tcal +/-5 degC, MATH NULL, fixed range (p. 12 footnote 5; p. 16 footnote 3; p. 20 footnote 5). Specifications are for PRESET; NPLC 100 (resistance: PRESET; NPLC 100; OCOMP ON; OHMF). AC volts, AC current and frequency print ONE column "24-hour to 2 year" (pp. 24, 27, 29, 32, 34): the same specification is stored under both periods.
notes.7: OPTION 002 (high stability, p. 12 footnote 5): the DC volts "ppm of reading" figures in parentheses are for Option 002 (only the DC volts table has parenthesised figures). PER THE OWNER the lab's 3458A HAS Option 002, so "Voltage, DC [Option 002 high stability]" is the DEFAULT of a plain DC volts lookup (specmanager.DEFAULT_VARIANT prefer "option 002"). The standard-stability figures (8 ppm / year) are stored as the alternate function "Voltage, DC [Standard stability]", selectable with variant="Standard stability". Ordering page: "8 ppm Stability" standard, "3458A-002 High stability (4 ppm/year) reference" option.
notes.8: DC VOLTS EXTRA TERMS, NOT STORED (p. 12): without MATH NULL add 0.15 ppm of range to 10 V, 0.7 ppm of range to 1 V and 7 ppm of range to 0.1 V; without MATH NULL and for a fixed range of less than 4 minutes add 0.25 ppm of range to 10 V, 1.7 ppm of range to 1 V and 17 ppm of range to 0.1 V. Footnote 6 (1000 V range): "Add 12 ppm X (Vin / 1000)2 additional errors for inputs > 100 vV" (printed so; read as 12 ppm x (Vin/1000)^2 of reading for inputs above 100 V: 12 ppm at 1000 V). Footnote 6 is NOT in any stored 1000 V row.
notes.9: DC VOLTS TRANSFER ACCURACY / LINEARITY (p. 13), stored under the period "10 min": 10 min, Tref +/-0.5 degC, ppm of reading + ppm of range: 100 mV 0.5 + 0.5, 1 V 0.3 + 0.1, 10 V 0.05 + 0.05, 100 V 0.5 + 0.1, 1000 V 1.5 + 0.05. Conditions (p. 13): following a 4-hour warm-up, full scale to 10 % of full scale; 1000 V range measurements within 5 % of the initial value and after settling; Tref is the starting ambient temperature; fixed range (> 4 min) using accepted metrology practices. A plain lookup (period "1 yr") never returns these rows; pass period="10 min".
notes.10: TWO-WIRE OHMS (p. 17): "add the following offset errors to the four-wire ohms (OHMF) accuracy: 24 Hour: 50 mOhm. 90 Day: 150 mOhm. 1 Year: 250 mOhm. 2 Year: 500 mOhm". Stored as a fixed term (0.05 / 0.15 / 0.25 / 0.5 ohm) added to the four-wire row, function "Resistance [2-wire (OHM)]". A plain resistance lookup prefers the 4-wire function (repository rule); pass variant="2-wire". 100 MOhm and 1 GOhm: the measurement is computed from 10 MOhm in parallel with the input (p. 16 footnote 4). OCOMP is stated ON for the accuracy table (p. 16 footnote 1); the data sheet lists the offset-compensated ohms for 10 Ohm to 100 kOhm only (p. 5), so the 1 MOhm to 1 GOhm rows cannot have OCOMP on (not explained in the data sheet).
notes.11: DC CURRENT TYPICAL (p. 20 footnote 6 "Typical accuracy"): the 100 nA, 1 uA and 10 uA rows are TYPICAL, not warranted; the labels say so. Factory traceability +5 ppm of reading is not in the rows (note 4). The range ends at 1.05 A (full scale): a current above 1.05 A (for example 2 A) has NO row and a lookup returns None; the maximum input is 1.5 A pk (p. 22).
notes.12: AC VOLTS: three techniques, one function each (p. 23): SETACV SYNC (synchronously sub-sampled, 1 Hz to 10 MHz, repetitive signal required), SETACV ANA (analog, 10 Hz to 2 MHz, power-up default), SETACV RNDM (random sampled, 20 Hz to 10 MHz). SYNC is split by ACBAND (<= 2 MHz and > 2 MHz, p. 24), RNDM likewise (p. 29); ANA has one table (p. 27). Accuracy is % of reading + % of range, 24 hour to 2 year. Conditions: SYNC and RNDM full scale to 10 % (SYNC) of full scale, ANA full scale to 1/20 full scale, DC < 10 % of the AC sine wave input, crest factor 1.4, PRESET, within 24 hours and +/-1 degC of the last ACAL, Lo to guard switch on, peak (AC + DC) input limited to 5 x full scale (SYNC); ANA: maximum DC 400 V. LFILTER ON recommended below 20 kHz (SYNC). A blank cell in the printed table means no specification: no row is stored (for example 10 mV at 300 kHz to 2 MHz, 1000 V above 100 kHz). The plain lookup returns the LARGEST limit of the modes that cover the point; pass variant="SYNC", "ANA" or "RNDM" (and "<= 2 MHz" / "> 2 MHz") for one mode. The RNDM table carries the footnote number 1 on its title, but its only footnote is the temperature-coefficient one: its own conditions are not printed (p. 29); the SYNC / ANA conditions are assumed to apply and that is UNVERIFIED.
notes.13: AC VOLTS TEMPERATURE COEFFICIENTS (% of reading + % of range per degC beyond +/-1 degC of the last ACAL but within +/-5 degC; information only): SYNC (p. 24) 10 mV 0.002 + 0.02, 100 mV - 1000 V 0.001 + 0.0001; ANA (p. 27) 10 mV 0.003 + 0.006 (specification applies full scale to 1/4 full scale), others 0.002 + 0.0; RNDM (p. 29) 10 mV 0.002 + 0.02, others 0.001 + 0.00001; for ACBAND > 2 MHz use the 10 mV figure for all ranges. High-frequency temperature coefficient (outside Tcal +/-5 degC, % of reading per degC, pp. 26, 31): 2-4 MHz 0.02 (10 mV - 1 V) / 0.08 (10 V - 1000 V); 4-10 MHz 0.08. AC current (p. 32): 0.002 + 0 for every range.
notes.14: AC CURRENT (p. 32): ACI and ACDCI, 24 hour to 2 year, % of reading + % of range, full scale to 1/20 full scale, sine wave, crest factor 1.4, PRESET, within 24 hours and +/-1 degC of the last ACAL. The 5 kHz to 20 kHz, 20 kHz to 50 kHz and 50 kHz to 100 kHz columns are TYPICAL (footnote 3; labels say so). The 100 uA range is limited to 1 kHz (footnote 4): the 100 Hz - 5 kHz cell is stored with its upper band edge at 1 kHz and its printed band in the label. Factory traceability +5 ppm of reading is not in the rows (note 4). The 1 A range is full scale 1.05 A.
notes.15: ADDITIONAL ERRORS, NOT STORED: noise (RMS noise multipliers and the NPLC curves, pp. 13, 14, 17, 19, 21), temperature coefficients of the DC functions (note 16), AZERO OFF temperature coefficient (DC volts 5 uV/degC on 100 mV - 10 V and 500 uV/degC on 100 V - 1000 V, p. 15; resistance, ppm of range per degC, p. 19: 10 and 100 ohm 50, 1 and 10 kohm 5, 100 kohm to 10 Mohm 1, 100 Mohm 10, 1 Gohm 100), low-frequency error, crest factor error, source-resistance flatness errors, resolution multipliers, ACDCV / ACDCI additional errors, settling, common mode rejection, reading rates, digitizing, math. The AC transfer accuracy (p. 24: 100 mV - 100 V, "0.002 + resolution in %" % of reading, 45 Hz - 20 kHz, within 10 min and +/-0.5 degC, 4-hour warm-up) depends on the RES setting and is NOT stored.
notes.16: DC TEMPERATURE COEFFICIENTS (ppm of reading + ppm of range per degC; without ACAL: additional error from Tcal or last ACAL +/-1 degC; with ACAL: from Tcal +/-5 degC; information only, read twice): DC volts (p. 12) 100 mV 1.2 + 1 / 0.15 + 1; 1 V 1.2 + 0.1 / 0.15 + 0.1; 10 V 0.5 + 0.01 / 0.15 + 0.01; 100 V 2 + 0.4 / 0.15 + 0.1; 1000 V 2 + 0.04 / 0.15 + 0.01. Resistance (p. 16) 10 and 100 ohm 3 + 1 / 1 + 1; 1, 10, 100 kohm 3 + 0.1 / 1 + 0.1; 1 Mohm 3 + 1 / 1 + 1; 10 Mohm 20 + 20 / 5 + 2; 100 Mohm 100 + 20 / 25 + 2; 1 Gohm 1000 + 20 / (not readable). DC current (p. 20) 100 nA 10 + 200 / 2 + 50; 1 uA 2 + 20 / 2 + 5; 10 uA 10 + 4 / 2 + 1; 100 uA 10 + 3 / 2 + 1; 1 mA 10 + 2 / 2 + 1; 10 mA 10 + 2 / 2 + 1; 100 mA 25 + 2 / 2 + 1; 1 A 25 + 3 / 2 + 2. Not in any stored row: the sheet is at the temperature conditions of note 6.
notes.17: FREQUENCY / PERIOD (p. 34): "24 Hour - 2 Year (0 degC - 55 degC)": 1 Hz - 40 Hz (1 s - 25 ms) 0.05 % of reading; 40 Hz - 100 MHz (25 ms - 100 ns) 0.01 % of reading. The same page lists the input ranges (voltage 1 Hz - 10 MHz, 700 V rms - 1 mV rms; current 1 Hz - 100 kHz, 1 A rms - 10 uA rms), so the printed 100 MHz upper limit of the accuracy table is beyond the voltage / current input range (not explained in the data sheet; stored as printed). Time base 10 MHz +/-0.01 %, 0 to 55 degC (p. 35). The period rows are the same table (periods in parentheses) and are not stored separately.
notes.18: DIRECTION: "input" - the 3458A measures (the 5790B / 8563E / 8902A sheets do the same). specmanager.StandardSpec.lookup defaults to direction "output" and the budget (uncertainty_budget.build) does not pass one, so use lookup(..., direction="input") / tartur.standard_accuracy(..., direction="input"). The Datasheet Builder matcher uses the row direction itself.
notes.19: RESOLUTION: the "Maximum Resolution" column of each function table is stored as the row resolution (source "manual"): 8.5 digits at NPLC 100. A measurement at fewer power line cycles has a larger resolution and larger noise (pp. 13, 14, 17, 19, 21: not stored).
